title: Choose the visual world for AiFoundIt search (re-roll 2, minimalist)
question: Every option is minimalist, and every card now shows a preview of the chat screen in that direction (hand-built HTML mocks). The roll assigned Station Clock.

options.label: Station Clock
options.lineage: Hans Hilfiker's Swiss railway clock: white face, black bars, one red disc
options.thesis: Black on white, with a single red disc that appears only where AiFoundIt found something.
options.viewport: Wordmark with a red disc, a row of tick marks showing indexing progress, the question right-aligned in bold, and the reply above a three-cell grid where the best match carries the red disc. A hairline move proposal sits below, with a black Move button.
options.risk: If the red disc gets used for anything other than 'found', the whole system loses its meaning.

raised.raise: One type size across the whole app; hierarchy comes only from weight and position.
No greys and no tints: black, white, and the one red.
States are printed marks: red disc = best match, hollow ring = also matches, filled tick = indexed.
Every division is a 1px black hairline. No shadows, no cards, no fills.
Results reflow in whole grid cells: 3 across on a phone, 5 on a tablet.
Thumbnails never shrink below a readable size; more results means more rows, not smaller cells.

options.label: E-ink Page
options.lineage: E-reader screens: warm grey ground, book serif, no color
options.thesis: Answers read like a quiet page of a book; files are listed like a table of contents.
options.viewport: Your question in italics, the answer in serif, files as listed entries with small dithered thumbnails, and an outlined Move button.
options.risk: Familiar and soft: it can feel drab, and the demo moment would be quiet.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Results as barcode columns and monospace data.
options.case: Loses on both: too dense and cold to be calm.

options.label: High-Density Modules
options.thesis: Packed boxed modules with red tabs.
options.case: Loses on both: the opposite of minimalist.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference
options.thesis: Twin text columns around a rail of keys.
options.viewport: Two columns with a center rail.
options.case: Loses on both: scholarly, and two columns don't fit a phone.

options.label: Convention Catalog
options.thesis: Hundreds of stamp-size thumbnails, circled in pen.
options.case: Loses on both: too dense, and it reads as a hobby reference.

options.label: Midnight Transit Map
options.thesis: Files as stations on colored lines.
options.case: Loses on both: colorful and forced.
options.kept: Never shrink content into an unreadable miniature.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: Every word at one type size, on slanted glass slides.
options.case: Loses on both: the slanted rack fights minimalism.
options.kept: One type size; hierarchy from weight only.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A standard AI chat app, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: The chat layout people already expect, with files as attachment rows.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Gemini or ChatGPT by design.
